title: COMP 3721 · Week 4
subtitle: Digital-to-digital conversion: line coding, preparing for Quiz 4
description: Lecture 04 and its complementary note: data elements and signal elements, data rate and signal rate, the bandwidth of a digital signal, baseline wandering, DC components, self-synchronization, and the line coding schemes (unipolar NRZ, polar NRZ-L and NRZ-I, Manchester, differential Manchester, bipolar AMI), with E04 worked. Every worked number from the slides and the exercise sheet, a live widget for each idea, and waveforms you draw yourself and check. Finish with Mock Quiz 4 and the Week 4 study note.
intro:
:::quiz Quiz 4 scope
The lab quizzes follow the lectures one week behind, so Quiz 4 is expected to cover Lecture 04, all of it in this module. The calculations are the signal rate and bandwidth formulas and the extra bits from a clock difference: write baud for a signal rate, bps for a data rate and Hz for a bandwidth. Be ready to turn a bit pattern into a signal, and a signal back into bits, for each scheme. One A4 or letter page of notes, single-sided and preferably hand-written, is allowed; the last lesson is the Week 4 block of that page.
:::

steps.note: take it cold first to find the gaps (about 35 min)
S = c × N × 1/r by hand, with r = 1, 1/2, 2 and 4/3; baud, not bps
the 0.1 percent example at 1 kbps and 1 Mbps
the level rules: unipolar, NRZ-L, NRZ-I, and the three problems of polar NRZ
0 is high-to-low, 1 is low-to-high; differential: inversion at the start for 0
draw every scheme for one pattern on paper, then in the widgets
hand-write the Week 4 block of your A4 page from this draft
